newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - IBM off, stocks seen weak.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - IBM off, stocks seen weak.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were called to open broadly lower, with bellwether International Business Machines Corp trading at 155-1/4, off from Tuesday's 158 close amid market rumors that IBM would soon issue a profit warning.
IBM said it had no comments on the rumors, and said it had no plans to issue a press release today.

The IBM speculation came as the market has shown fierce resilience following Friday morning's steep sell-off. Analysts said stocks were vulnerable to a correction following their snapback since Friday afternoon.
Traders said Intel Corp was trading at 128-3/4, off from Tuesday's 129-1/8 finish.
They said activity in the pre-open was moderate.
Meanwhile, HMT Technology Corp was trading at 14-3/4, off from Tuesday's 15-7/8 end. The company late Tuesday warned that earnings for the December 31 quarter would fall below consensus expectations.
As for Wednesday's anticipated ugly opening, one trader remarked, "They're looking for excuses to take us down."
He cited the IBM speculation and unsubstantiated rumors that Goldman Sach's Abby Joseph Cohen was lowering her weighting on stocks and that the Japanese were selling 30-year bonds.
